label: Trend Hunt
thesis: Find persistent trends early and lean on price action to stay in motion.
summaryBullets: Discovery favors trend scans and relative-strength leaders.
Evidence leans price-action first with confirmation.
Catalysts help but are not mandatory.
Fundamentals only need a sanity check.

whatToLookFor: Relative-strength leaders, clean continuation names, and instruments already showing trend persistence.
Catalysts that strengthen an existing move without requiring a full event-driven thesis.
howToEvaluate: Lead with price action and structure first, then use narrative as confirmation.
Reject weak or lagging names even if the story sounds good.
Use fundamentals mainly as a sanity check, not as the primary conviction source.

label: Catalyst Momentum
thesis: Chase clean momentum only when fresh catalysts can keep attention and volume alive.
summaryBullets: Discovery starts from catalyst and news scans.
Evidence balances narrative with tape confirmation.
Catalysts are required, not optional.
Fundamentals only need a quick sanity check.

whatToLookFor: Fresh catalysts, breaking news, and event-driven attention with immediate reaction potential.
Names where the catalyst is concrete and current rather than speculative.
howToEvaluate: Do not advance ideas without a real catalyst.
Balance narrative with tape confirmation so the setup is not just story-driven.
Keep the fundamental pass light and time-sensitive unless it directly changes the catalyst read.

label: Institutional Quality
thesis: Wait for durable, high-quality names and demand stronger confirmation before committing.
summaryBullets: Discovery starts from curated quality watchlists.
Evidence favors confirmation before action.
Catalysts are optional unless they strengthen the case.
Fundamental review is deep, not cursory.

whatToLookFor: Liquid, high-quality names with credible institutional characteristics and durable narratives.
Setups that remain sensible beyond short-lived hype.
howToEvaluate: Require stronger confirmation than usual before elevating a candidate.
Do not promote low-quality speculation just because it is active.
Use deeper business-quality and durability confirmation as part of the decision, not just a light screen.

label: Mean Reversion Dislocation
thesis: Hunt overstretched moves where odds favor a snap-back once panic or euphoria cools.
summaryBullets: Discovery looks for dislocations and exhaustion.
Evidence waits for reversal confirmation.
Catalysts are usually not required.
Fundamentals are a light sanity filter.

whatToLookFor: Overextended moves, panic/euphoria, and credible dislocations likely to revert.
Names showing early signs that exhaustion is turning into stabilization or reversal.
howToEvaluate: Require reversal confirmation before upgrading conviction.
Do not mistake strong continuation for a mean-reversion setup.

label: Prediction Event Edge
thesis: Trade event contracts where evidence can shift implied probabilities before resolution.
summaryBullets: Discovery focuses on event contracts and resolution timelines.
Evidence is probability-edge first.
Catalysts are required because event flow drives repricing.
Fundamentals are usually not applicable.

whatToLookFor: Event contracts, resolution criteria, and incoming evidence that can shift implied odds.
Current facts that create measurable probability-edge opportunities.
howToEvaluate: Think in terms of mispriced odds instead of standard equity momentum.
Require explicit event relevance and catalyst flow before escalating a candidate.
Treat traditional fundamentals as mostly irrelevant unless they directly affect resolution odds.

label: Custom Style
thesis: Blend your own discovery and evidence posture.
summaryBullets: No preset assumptions beyond what you set below.
Use style notes to define the edge clearly.

howToEvaluate: Lean on the live session notes and explicit field values because no built-in style assumptions should dominate.
